anti_template_constraints: Do not use a KPI strip, chart wall, generic card grid, or sidebar-first dashboard as the primary authenticated experience.
Do not split one request into unrelated tabs that hide the source request while evidence, assignment, visit, or readiness work is active.
Do not present status as decoration. Pair every state with the accountable actor, retained evidence, and next permitted command.
Do not use placeholder copy, dead actions, unlabeled icons, fake activity, invented response-time promises, or unverified outcome claims.
Do not expose command ids, schema versions, factory stages, build metadata, provider configuration, raw policy expressions, or secrets in customer screens.
Do not color-code readiness without a text label, checklist result, decision-maker, time, and evidence references.
Do not imply that quote-ready means a quote was issued, accepted, won, or paid.

composition.authenticated_workspace: A quiet workbench built around one vertical request spine. The source request stays in the center, retained evidence clips to the left rail, accountable decisions stitch down the right seam, and one permission-aware next move rests at the bottom. Queue views use compact rows that open directly into this dossier rather than a dashboard of detached cards.
composition.public_entry: An anonymous estimate-request sheet explains what the company needs, why each detail helps, what will happen after submission, and that a human will review the request. It keeps company operations, staff notes, and readiness controls out of the public experience.

design_contract.experience_thesis: QuoteRivet should feel like assembling one trustworthy job file, not monitoring a sales dashboard. The source request forms a fixed spine. Evidence, field facts, accountable decisions, and handoff receipts attach to that spine in order, so anyone can see what changed, who decided, what still blocks progress, and the one permitted next move.
design_contract.interaction_metaphor: A riveted request dossier with a fixed spine, clipped evidence rail, stitched decision seam, and a single next-move dock.

signature_interactions.description: Opening any queue item anchors the source request in the center while assignment, evidence, field facts, readiness, and handoff attach around it. Switching work modes never replaces the active request with a generic dashboard.
signature_interactions.name: Follow the request spine

signature_interactions.description: Selecting a readiness criterion reveals only the exact current evidence versions that support it. A result cannot be recorded until the reviewer addresses missing, disputed, restricted, or stale evidence.
signature_interactions.name: Stitch evidence to a decision

signature_interactions.description: The bottom dock presents one command allowed by current state, permission, policy, and revision. It explains blocked guards in customer language and sends authority questions to the named human role.
signature_interactions.name: One guarded next move

signature_interactions.description: The handoff compacts the current readiness decision, evidence refs, limitations, recipient access, and open obligations into an immutable receipt. Later changes visibly invalidate the seal without erasing transfer or acknowledgement history.
signature_interactions.name: Seal and receive the handoff

visual_language.color_system: Use warm paper and graphite neutrals for the dossier, oxidized copper for the active stitch and focus ring, field blue for links and neutral progress, amber for unresolved checks, and brick red for stopped work. Every color has a text label and icon. Meet WCAG AA contrast in all states and never use color alone to signal readiness.
visual_language.data_visualization: Use a thin chronological stitch for attributable events, compact checklist rows for evidence coverage, and queue aging as labeled elapsed time. Do not add charts without retained source data, a decision they support, and an accessible table equivalent.
visual_language.shape_language: A strong vertical spine, offset clipped rails, narrow stitched connectors, square evidence thumbnails, and a rounded bottom command dock. Use borders and spacing to show attachment and version lineage. Avoid a uniform field of floating rounded cards.
visual_language.typography: Use a sturdy humanist sans for instructions and controls, tabular numerals for times and versions, and a restrained slab or serif accent only for request identifiers and section folios. Preserve 16px body text, 1.5 line height, visible focus, 44px touch targets, and readable layout at 200 percent zoom.

forbidden_scaffold_phrases: Share the workflow and team context.
promotion_rule: Source publication and deployment are blocked until an independent design-quality reviewer approves all required screenshots and scripts/verify-design-readiness.py passes.

anti_bloat_rules: Show one request and one primary next move at a time.
Keep history collapsed until the user asks for prior versions or decisions.
Put advanced policy, retention, archive, restore, restriction, and invalidation controls behind a named More actions disclosure.
Use queue rows for comparison and the dossier for action. Do not duplicate full forms inside cards.
Never display implementation metadata as a customer-facing panel.

primary_modes.label: Request
primary_modes.purpose: Review or correct the source request while its identity and current state stay visible.

primary_modes.label: Evidence
primary_modes.purpose: Capture or review evidence and site facts without losing the active request.

primary_modes.label: Decision
primary_modes.purpose: Review the current decision trail and execute one guarded next command.

advanced_controls: invalidate a prior decision or handoff

save_behavior.status_feedback: Show Saving beside the edited section, then Saved with the latest revision. A command result must name the new state and accountable next step. A stale revision keeps the user's draft and asks them to review the changed facts before retrying.
